correctness.rationale: The lattice calculation is correct. For an even hyperbolic rank-two lattice, the least positive value of the half-intersection form satisfies \(m^2\le\Delta\) by the same reduction used in the inspected 2026 primary source. Hence \(\Delta<16\) forces a primitive class of square 2, 4, or 6 and therefore one of the polarization types yielding irrationality degree 3. For \(U(4)\), every norm is a multiple of 8, so squares 2,4,6,12 are absent, while the pairing ideal is \(4\mathbb Z\) and contains 12. The inspected verifier also checks the determinant, primitive positive vector, and primitive embedding into \(U^3\). Standard period-map realization then gives generic abelian surfaces with exact Neron-Severi lattice \(U(4)\).

originality.rationale: The decisive ingredients are already present in stronger prior results. Huang-Jiang-Yang give the complete degree-of-irrationality classification by polarization type and, in the proof of their lattice lemma, explicitly derive the same inequality \(m^2\le\Delta\). Combining those statements immediately gives \(\Delta<16\Rightarrow m\le3\Rightarrow\operatorname{irr}=3\). At equality, \(U(4)\) is the standard rank-two even hyperbolic lattice with norms divisible by 8, and standard abelian-surface period theory realizes it. Martin already supplies the 12-intersection obstruction. Thus the advertised discriminant-16 threshold and 'first gap beyond Martin' are a routine synthesis/corollary of stronger published ingredients rather than an independent new theorem.
